question: Why are pyroclastic flows deadlier than the eruption column itself?
answer: While the eruption column is hot and light, it rises. When its top cools and grows heavier, it falls back and races along the ground as a glowing cloud at hundreds of km/h, scorching whatever it reaches.
move: The worst danger is not the column going up, but the column coming down.

web.label: Diagram of a vertical volcanic eruption column with a switch. Flipping it cools the column's top so it turns heavy and falls into a fast, ground-hugging glowing cloud. Asks why pyroclastic flows are deadlier than the eruption column.
